text:
I’m a tourist from France, and before coming to New York, I did some research on the places you supposedly “shouldn’t miss.” Joe’s Pizza at 1435 Broadway was one of them.
I had seen information suggesting that pizza slices were around $2. Let me be very clear: that was absolutely not my experience.
As a European and someone familiar with Italian food, I know what a simple cheese pizza is supposed to be: straightforward, good-quality ingredients, proper cheese, and a good crust. What I was served here was honestly disgusting. The cheese was like mush, the quality was extremely disappointing, and it was nothing like the famous New York pizza experience I had been expecting.
What bothered me even more was the feeling that tourists are simply there to be rushed through, served whatever they are given, and charged. I did not feel welcomed or valued as a customer at all. It felt like: pay, eat, and get out.
Maybe Joe’s Pizza earned its reputation many years ago, but I’m writing this review as a tourist visiting New York in 2026, and based on my personal experience, I simply do not understand the hype.
For such a famous name, serving pizza of this quality and treating tourists this way is a real shame.
Very disappointing experience. I cannot recommend this place, and personally, I would avoid it.

text:
A truly wonderful evening! We had the pleasure of dining at the Chef's Table with wine pairings and were delighted from the first course to the last.

The dishes were superbly prepared, creative, and meticulously crafted. The wine pairings were excellently selected and complemented each course perfectly.

We were particularly impressed by the cohesive overall concept. The owner's handcrafted pottery perfectly complements the dishes and adds a special touch to the experience. The open fire, where some of the food is prepared, beautifully completes the concept and creates a unique atmosphere.

But what truly made the evening special was the warm hospitality. The entire team was attentive, friendly, and genuine. You feel welcome from the moment you arrive and simply have a fantastic time.

Even the restrooms are something special – exceptionally designed, original, and with great attention to detail. They, too, contribute to a complete experience that is thoughtfully planned down to the smallest detail.

text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We visited a Michelin-starred restaurant for the first time on **July 23, 2026**, and honestly, we couldn't have chosen a better place.

From the moment you step into Hallmann & Klee, you can tell that the people who work here love their job. You feel welcome from the very first moment, not like a guest who has simply reserved a table.

Sarah Hallmann is ever-present – ​​close to the guests and right in the thick of things. Her warm, natural manner is infectious and, together with the entire team, creates an atmosphere where you immediately feel at ease. The service is attentive, professional, and pleasantly relaxed. Every course and every drink is presented with palpable passion, without ever seeming forced.

The menu was a true journey of discovery for us. Each course had its own character, yet everything came together to form a harmonious whole. We were particularly impressed by how even seemingly simple ingredients like potatoes or a Hawaiian toast could be transformed into something extraordinary. You can taste the creativity, the craftsmanship, and above all, the attention to detail in every single dish. Each course was perfectly balanced, full of surprising flavors, and prepared with a precision that never ceased to amaze us. The dishes never felt overloaded, but rather clear, harmonious, and meticulously thought out down to the smallest detail.

We were equally impressed by the beverage pairings. We opted for both the wine pairing and the non-alcoholic option. To be honest, we had expected the drinks to simply complement the food. In fact, they were an integral part of the experience. Each pairing seemed to enhance the flavors of the dishes, revealing new facets and further elevating the enjoyment. The selection was exceptionally discerning, creative, and perfectly coordinated. We have never before experienced such a sophisticated beverage pairing – both with and without alcohol.

We also loved the ambiance. The restaurant's design is deliberately understated, and that's precisely what gives it its charm. Nothing distracts from what truly matters: the people, the cuisine, and the shared culinary experience.

Many thanks to Sarah Hallmann, the entire service team, and the kitchen for this wonderful evening. If this was our first visit to a Michelin-starred restaurant, then you've set the bar incredibly high. We'll be thinking about this evening for a long time and will definitely be back.

Finally, a recommendation for anyone who might feel the same way we did: If you've had any reservations about fine dining, just let them go. Trust the team at Hallmann & Klee and embrace this experience. It's not about navigating a supposedly exclusive world, but about being welcomed with genuine warmth and enjoying exceptional cuisine. For us, there couldn't have been a better place to take our first step into the world of Michelin-starred dining.
originalText:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Wir waren am **23.07.2026** zum ersten Mal in einem Sternerestaurant und ehrlich gesagt hätten wir uns keinen besseren Ort dafür aussuchen können.

Schon beim Betreten des Hallmann & Klee merkt man, dass hier Menschen arbeiten, die ihren Beruf lieben. Man fühlt sich vom ersten Moment an willkommen und nicht wie ein Gast, der einfach nur einen Tisch reserviert hat.

*Sarah Hallmann* ist dabei ständig präsent – nah am Gast und mitten im Geschehen. Ihre herzliche, natürliche Art steckt an und schafft gemeinsam mit dem gesamten Team eine Atmosphäre, in der man sich sofort wohlfühlt. Der Service ist aufmerksam, professionell und dabei angenehm ungezwungen. Jeder Gang und jedes Getränk werden mit spürbarer Leidenschaft präsentiert, ohne dabei jemals aufgesetzt zu wirken.

Das Menü war für uns eine echte Entdeckungsreise. Jeder Gang hatte seinen eigenen Charakter und dennoch ergab am Ende alles ein stimmiges Ganzes. Besonders beeindruckt hat uns, dass selbst scheinbar einfache Zutaten wie Kartoffeln oder ein Toast Hawaii zu etwas Außergewöhnlichem werden können. Man schmeckt die Kreativität, das handwerkliche Können und vor allem die Liebe zum Detail in jedem einzelnen Teller. Jeder Gang war perfekt ausbalanciert, voller überraschender Aromen und mit einer Präzision zubereitet, die uns immer wieder staunen ließ. Die Gerichte wirkten dabei nie überladen, sondern klar, harmonisch und bis ins kleinste Detail durchdacht.

Mindestens genauso begeistert waren wir von der Getränkebegleitung. Wir hatten sowohl die Weinbegleitung als auch die alkoholfreie Variante gewählt. Ehrlich gesagt hatten wir erwartet, dass die Getränke einfach gut zu den Speisen passen würden. Tatsächlich waren sie aber ein gleichwertiger Teil des Menüs. Jede einzelne Begleitung schien die Aromen der Gerichte weiterzuerzählen, neue Facetten hervorzubringen und den Genuss noch einmal zu steigern. Die Auswahl war außergewöhnlich sensibel, kreativ und perfekt abgestimmt. Eine so raffinierte Getränkebegleitung – sowohl mit als auch ohne Alkohol – haben wir bisher noch nicht erlebt.

Auch das Ambiente hat uns sehr gefallen. Das Restaurant ist bewusst schlicht gestaltet und genau das macht seinen Charme aus. Nichts lenkt vom Wesentlichen ab: den Menschen, der Küche und dem gemeinsamen Genusserlebnis.

Vielen Dank an Sarah Hallmann, das gesamte Serviceteam und die Küche für diesen wunderbaren Abend. Wenn dies unser erster Besuch in einem Sternerestaurant war, dann habt ihr die Messlatte verdammt hoch gelegt. Wir werden noch oft an diesen Abend denken und kommen ganz bestimmt wieder.

Zum Schluss noch eine Empfehlung an alle, denen es vielleicht so geht wie uns: Falls ihr bisher Berührungsängste mit der Sternegastronomie hattet, legt sie einfach ab. Vertraut euch dem Team von Hallmann & Klee an und lasst euch auf dieses Erlebnis ein. Hier geht es nicht darum, sich in einer vermeintlich exklusiven Welt zurechtzufinden, sondern darum, mit echter Herzlichkeit empfangen zu werden und außergewöhnliche Küche zu genießen. Für uns hätte es keinen besseren Ort geben können, um den ersten Schritt in die Welt der Sternegastronomie zu machen.

placeAddress: Vorwerck Restaurant - Dine & Show, Karl-Marx-Straße 131, 12043 Berlin, Germany
text:
We were there for the first time on August 8th, 2026, for our wedding anniversary. Apparently, we weren't expected (shocked looks and an empty restaurant) despite our reservation. But Chef Roman (Klausi 😉) had everything prepared in 5 minutes, just as we had agreed upon, while we enjoyed a drink at the bar. In the private room (which was provided to us free of charge), the menu was explained to us in detail and very professionally. We had the 5-course Chef's Candlelight Dinner (my wife had the lamb and I had the veal fillet), which Marius had recommended. Each course was accompanied by a perfectly paired drink in beautiful tumblers and glasses provided by Klausi, which were always just right. We were able to request songs from Dave and enjoyed dancing to them live. As the grand finale, and after dessert (crème brûlée with the perfectly complementary apple-rhubarb compote), we danced to our song. And yes, we were the only ones at Vorwerk all evening... which made it even more unforgettable. All in all, we can highly recommend Vorwerck for any occasion – an evening to enjoy, forget about time, feast, play games, dance, and much more!

Thanks to the whole team for this unforgettable evening!
originalText:
Waren 08.08.26 zu unserem  Hochzeitstag zum ersten Mal da . Scheinbar wurden wir nicht erwartet ( geschokte Blicke und leeres Restaurant ) trotz Reservierung. Aber Küchenchef Roman ( Klausi 😉 ) hat in 5 min alles vorbereitet was abgemacht war. Während wir an der Bar ein Drink genossen . Uns wurde  im separee ( was  uns kostenfrei zur Verfügung gestellt wurde ) ausführlich und professionell das Menü erklärt . Wir hatten das 5 Gang Chefs Candlelight Dinner( meine Frau hatte das Lamm und ich das Kalbsfilet ) was mir Marius empfohlen hatte . Es gab zum jeden Gang ein korrespondierenden Drink in tollen Tumbler und Gläser von Klausi, die immer passten . Wir konnten uns bei Dave Musik Titel wünschen und genossen Sie live tanzend . Zum krönenden Abschluss und nach dem  Dessert ( Crème Brûlée mit den sehr gut passenden Apfel - Rhabarber Kompott ),  tanzten wir zu unserem Lied. Und  ja wir waren den ganzen Abend Alleine im Vorwerk.... Was es noch unvergesslicher machte . Alles im allen können wir das Vorwerck für jeden Anlass um ein Abend zum Genießen ,Zeit vergessen , Schlemmen , Spielen ,Tanzen und noch vieles mehr, empfehlen!
Danke an das ganze Team für diesen unvergesslichen Abend!
ownerResponseText:
To be honest, the beginning of your evening was our fault, and I'd rather be honest about it than sugarcoat it. You had booked, we weren't prepared, and the looks you described were exactly what they seemed. That it still turned into an evening you're writing about is all thanks to Roman; he transformed five minutes of chaos into a wedding day. We've looked into how it happened so that the next first visit with us will start differently. Thank you for giving us the chance to salvage the evening instead of leaving right away. All the best to you both 💍

Warm regards, Marius, Ela, Roman, and the entire Vorwerck Team
ownerResponseOriginalText:
Ganz ehrlich, der Anfang eures Abends war unser Fehler, und ich schreibe das hier lieber offen als schön. Ihr wart angemeldet, wir waren nicht darauf eingestellt, und die Blicke, die du beschreibst, waren genau das, wonach sie aussahen. Dass daraus trotzdem ein Abend geworden ist, über den ihr so schreibt, ist Romans Verdienst, er hat aus fünf Minuten Chaos einen Hochzeitstag gemacht. Wir haben uns intern angesehen, wie es dazu kommen konnte, damit der nächste erste Besuch bei uns anders anfängt. Danke, dass ihr uns die Chance gelassen habt, den Abend noch zu drehen, statt gleich wieder zu gehen. Alles Gute euch beiden 💍

placeAddress: KÖK Berlin - Modern Anatolian Restaurant, Karl-Marx-Straße 283, 12057 Berlin, Germany
text: A clear five stars "plus" for this hidden gem in the heart of Neukölln. In a sophisticated, spacious atmosphere – you'll find few places in Berlin with more of a "Manhattan" feel – dishes are served. From stuffed, dried vegetables to sweetbreads with broad beans, traditional dishes are given a modern and contemporary twist, presented beautifully, even perfectly. Thoughtfully designed, visually Instagrammable, but not pretentious – simply delicious. Even the filled chocolate mousse had its own elegant touch. Once the relevant food critics discover this place, a hype is guaranteed. The fact that the server might be somewhat of a newcomer to the industry is no problem, as it's more than compensated for by her charm and friendliness. Tip: If you can't or don't want to eat large portions, one or two appetizers will easily suffice.
originalText: Glasklar fünf Sterne „plus“ gibt es hier für diesen Geheimtipp in der Tiefe Neuköllns. Bei gefüllten, getrockneten Gemüsen und Kalbsbries mit Saubohnen werden traditionelle Gerichte modern und zeitgemäß aufgebohrt und optisch wunderschön, ja perfekt serviert. text:
We had the 7-course dinner at Merold and it was absolutely fantastic — a true highlight of our time in Berlin.
The standout dishes for me were the hake with hake caviar, the creative reinterpretation of shallot, buckwheat, and black garlic, the beautifully executed Spätzle and lentils, the house-made Bratwurst, and the tender rabbit dish. Every plate showed thoughtful technique, excellent ingredients, and real creativity while staying true to modern German roots.
As a sommelier, I was especially impressed by the wine pairings. Being in Berlin, I discovered several outstanding German wines here that were completely new to me — the 2022 Heerkretz Sauvignon Blanc from Tomislav Markovic, the Niklas Rückrich Spätburgunder, and the Lingenfelder Satyr Blanc de Noirs were all exceptional. The pairing elevated the entire meal.
A big thank you to Jonas and the whole team at Merold for the warm, knowledgeable service and such a memorable culinary experience. We’ll definitely be back!

placeAddress: merold, Pannierstraße 24, 12047 Berlin-Bezirk Neukölln, Germany
text:
Yesterday I ate at Merold in Neukölln and went home with a really good feeling. I grew up in southern Germany, and the food brought back many wonderful memories of my childhood cuisine – but in a modern and very successful way.

Jonas' signature dishes, in particular, are simply amazing:

Onion with buckwheat and black garlic is a truly powerful dish. Simple on the plate, but with fantastic depth and flavor.

The homemade bratwurst was the most aromatic bratwurst I've ever had!

It's great that they always offer seasonal variations.

What particularly struck me was the newly built cellar, a veritable laboratory for fermentation. You can taste the work in every dish – the fermented ingredients give the food a beautiful depth and freshness without seeming artificial. This fits perfectly with the whole concept of regional ingredients from Berlin and Brandenburg and a lot of craftsmanship.

The restaurant is bright and inviting, the seating is comfortable, and you can relax and have a good conversation.

Jonas Merold is often in the dining room himself and is very welcoming.

Thank you so much for the wonderful evening. The dishes reminded me of home, but on a higher and more creative level. Definitely order the wine pairing. It elevates every dish to the stars 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
I'll gladly come back and highly recommend Merold.

Keep up the great work!
originalText:
Gestern war ich im Merold in Neukölln essen und bin mit einem richtig guten Gefühl nach Hause gegangen. Ich bin in Süddeutschland aufgewachsen, und das Essen hat viele schöne Erinnerungen an die Küche meiner Kindheit geweckt – nur auf eine moderne und sehr gelungene Art.

Insbesondere die Signature-Gerichte von Jonas sind einfach der Wahnsinn:
Zwiebel mit Buchweizen und schwarzem Knoblauch ist ein richtig starkes Gericht. Schlicht auf dem Teller, aber mit toller Tiefe und Geschmack.
Die hausgemachte Bratwurst  war aromatisch die geilste Bratwurst meines Lebens!
Schön, dass sie immer wieder mit saisonalen Varianten kommt.
Was mir besonders aufgefallen ist: Der neu gebaute Keller ist ein richtiges Labor für Fermentation. Man merkt diese Arbeit in jedem Gang – die fermentierten Zutaten geben dem Essen eine schöne Tiefe und Frische, ohne dass es aufgesetzt wirkt. Das passt sehr gut zum ganzen Konzept mit regionalen Zutaten aus Berlin und Brandenburg und viel Handwerk.
Das Restaurant ist klar und angenehm eingerichtet, man sitzt gut und kann sich entspannt und gut unterhalten.

placeAddress: merold, Pannierstraße 24, 12047 Berlin-Bezirk Neukölln, Germany
text:
Why this restaurant is recommended by the Michelin Guide or awarded 87 Falstaff points is beyond me.

The enigmatic list of unusually combined ingredients on the menu raises hopes for sophisticated, imaginative, and intensely flavorful dishes. Unfortunately, the kitchen fails to live up to these expectations in any way—with the possible exception of the first appetizer, the pike herring.

All subsequent courses ranged from mediocre to bland, and some combinations were definitely incongruous (e.g., the dessert).

The highlight of the "signature dish," a bratwurst in a roll (the first bite resulted in a large quantity of, presumably fermented, mustard seeds spilling onto the plate), was the roll itself. The Franconian version, known as "3 im Weggla," tastes far superior and costs nowhere near €16!

It's also worth mentioning that the individual portions are so small that even seven courses would hardly satisfy the average diner.

The restaurant's decor isn't minimalist Scandinavian; it's more reminiscent of a school cafeteria.

On the positive side, all three servers were very courteous, friendly, and attentive.

Unfortunately, neither the quality nor the price was justified, but the woke Berlin crowd didn't seem to notice, leaving full of praise for the delicious meal.
originalText:
Warum das Restaurant vom Guide Michelin empfohlen wird oder 87 Falstaff-Punkte erhält ist mir schleierhaft.

Die rätselhafte Auflistung ungewöhnlich zusammengestellter Zutaten auf der Speisekarte lässt auf ausgefallene, ideenreiche und geschmacksintensive Gerichte hoffen. Leider erfülltt die Küche die geschürten Erwartungen aber in keiner Weise - mit Ausnahme vielleicht der ersten Vorspeise, dem Hechtmatjes.

Alle weiteren Gänge waren mittelmäßig bis langweilig, manche in den Zusammenstellungen definitiv unstimmig (z.B. das Dessert).

Beim "Signature Dish", Bratwurst im Brötchen (beim ersten Bissen fiel eine große Menge, vermutlich fermentierte, Senfkörner auf den Teller). war das Brötchen das Highlight. Das in Franken als "3 im Weggla" bezeichnete Vorbild schmeckt allemal besser und kostet bei Weitem keine 16€!

Erwähnenswert ist noch, dass die einzelnen Portionen so klein ausfallen, dass ein durchschnittlicher Esser auch von sieben Gängen kaum satt werden kann.

Die Einrichtung des Lokals ist nicht skandinavisch reduziert, sondern erinnert eher an eine Schulmensa.

Positiv zu erwähnen ist, dass alle drei Mitarbeiter im Service sehr zuvorkommend, freundlich und aufmerksam waren.

Leider stimmen hier weder die Leistung, noch der dafür aufgerufene Preis, doch das woke Berliner Publikum scheint dies nicht zu erkennen, sondern verabschiedet sich voll des Lobes für das feine Mahl..

placeAddress: Mann - o - Salwa, Karl-Marx-Straße 223, 12055 Berlin, Germany
text:
⭐ Review

Disappointing and far from an authentic Malai Kofta

I ordered Malai Kofta expecting a dish with the complexity, creaminess, and richness of flavors typical of Indian/Pakistani cuisine. Unfortunately, what I received fell far short of what I understand as an authentic Malai Kofta.

For €11.50, the dish basically consisted of two vegetable croquettes smothered in a very thin, flavorless sauce, whose main appeal seemed to be simply the orange color of the curry. The sauce lacked depth, spices, and creaminess.

Furthermore, the koftas didn't have the composition I expected from this dish: there was no paneer or significant presence of nuts, elements that usually add texture and richness to this type of preparation. Instead, they were more like simple vegetable croquettes.

The rice was also subpar: sticky and clumpy, far from good basmati rice, which should be loose and fluffy.

The salad didn't seem particularly fresh either. The lettuce was limp and lacked the crispness of a freshly prepared salad, giving the impression that it had been sitting out for quite some time.

Overall, for €11.50, I expected much more. I ended up paying for two vegetable croquettes, a watery sauce with practically no flavor, and boiled rice.

It's a shame, because Indian and Pakistani cuisine has an enormous wealth of flavors, spices, textures, and techniques. In this case, the dish seemed too Westernized and simplified, as if the ingredients and preparation had been reduced to a minimum to cut costs and maximize profit.

I wouldn't recommend stopping at this restaurant if you're looking for authentic Indian/Pakistani food. If you've tried a good Malai Kofta, the difference will probably be very obvious.

Friendly waiter, good service…
originalText:
⭐ Reseña

Decepcionante y muy alejado de un auténtico Malai Kofta

Pedí un Malai Kofta esperando encontrar un plato con la complejidad, cremosidad y riqueza de sabores propia de la cocina india/pakistaní. Lamentablemente, lo que recibí estuvo muy lejos de lo que entiendo por un auténtico Malai Kofta.

Por 11,50 €, el plato consistía básicamente en dos croquetas de verduras bañadas en una salsa muy líquida, con poco o ningún sabor, cuyo principal atractivo parecía ser simplemente el color anaranjado del curry. La salsa carecía de profundidad, especias y cremosidad.

Además, las koftas no tenían la composición que esperaba de este plato: no se apreciaba paneer ni una presencia significativa de frutos secos, elementos que suelen aportar textura y riqueza a este tipo de preparación. En su lugar, resultaban más parecidas a unas simples croquetas de verduras.

El arroz tampoco estaba a la altura: pegajoso y apelmazado, muy lejos de un buen arroz basmati, que debería quedar suelto y graneado.

La ensalada tampoco parecía especialmente fresca. La lechuga estaba blanda y sin el punto crujiente de una ensalada recién preparada, dando la impresión de haber estado bastante tiempo expuesta.

En conjunto, por 11,50 € esperaba mucho más. Terminé pagando por dos croquetas de verduras, una salsa aguada con sabor prácticamente inexistente y arroz hervido.

Es una pena, porque la cocina india y pakistaní tiene una enorme riqueza de sabores, especias, texturas y técnicas. En este caso, el plato me pareció demasiado occidentalizado y simplificado, como si se hubieran reducido los ingredientes y la elaboración al mínimo para abaratar costes y maximizar el rendimiento.

No recomendaría detenerse en este restaurante si lo que buscas es comida india/pakistaní auténtica. Si has probado un buen Malai Kofta, la diferencia probablemente te resultará muy evidente.

placeDescription: Intimate eatery offering classic Yemeni plates & slow-cooked meats in a brick-walled dining area.
text:
Here, your taste buds are taken on a culinary journey to Yemen. The food is very authentic and impresses with traditional flavors.

Ordering and payment are done via a digital menu using a credit card or PayPal. It's a little unusual that you pay first and then eat. Alternatively, you can also order and pay directly at the counter.

The stews, served in clay bowls with fresh bread, are especially recommended. The lemon juice with mint perfectly complements the meal.

Those with a big appetite can order the whole lamb.
originalText:
Hier werden die Geschmacksknospen auf eine kulinarische Reise in den Jemen entführt. Das Essen ist sehr authentisch und überzeugt mit traditionellen Aromen.

Bestellung und Bezahlung erfolgen über eine digitale Speisekarte per Kreditkarte oder PayPal. Etwas ungewohnt ist, dass man zuerst bezahlt und dann isst. Alternativ kann man auch direkt am Tresen bestellen und bezahlen.

Besonders empfehlenswert sind die Eintöpfe, die in Tontellern serviert werden und mit frischem Brot gereicht werden. Der Zitronensaft mit Minze rundet das Essen perfekt ab.

Wer großen Hunger hat bestellt das ganze Lamm.

text:
I visited again after some time. It's not what it used to be. I'm sorry I can't give a better review because I like the owner. The prices are generally okay.

What was lacking was the food itself. The Wiener Schnitzel was barely edible, not at all crispy, the breading was soggy and stuck to the schnitzel, and tasted like flour – perhaps it wasn't cooked hot enough? In any case, it's not what you'd expect from a schnitzel specialist.

The small pork schnitzel was also completely flat and made a similarly unappealing impression. Even our child was disappointed.

The potato salad that accompanied the schnitzel was a complete disaster. It seems they dice pre-cooked potatoes from a catering supplier – the same kind they also serve as fried potatoes – and dress them haphazardly. Anyone who's ever had a decent potato salad in Bavaria or Austria would give this a failing grade. This definitely needs to be investigated.


The small pork schnitzel was also completely flat and made a similarly unappealing impression. It's a shame, we used to enjoy coming here, but not anymore. It might be enough for tourists, but it no longer appeals to us.
originalText:
Nach einiger Zeit mal wieder besucht. Nicht mehr das, was es mal war. Tut mir leid, keine bessere Betreuung zu schreiben, weil mir der Wirt sympathisch ist. Die Preise sind grundsätzlich ok.

Was nicht passte, war das Essen an sich. Das Wiener Schnitzel war grad so genießbar, überhaupt nicht souffliert, die Pannade klebte labbrig am Schnitzel und schmeckte nach Mehl - vielleicht nicht heiß genug gebacken? Jedenfalls für einen Schnitzel-Spezialisten kein Aushängeschild.

Das kleine Schnitzel vom Schwein war auch ganz platt und machte einen ähnlich ungünstigen Eindruck. Selbst unser Kind war enttäuscht.

Der das Schnitzel begleitende Kartoffelsalat war ein Offenbarungseid. Hier werden wohl vorgekochte Kartoffeln vom Gastrolieferanten, die im selben Kaliber übrigens auch als Bratkartoffeln kredenzt werden, gewürfelt und irgendwie angemacht. Jeder, der schon einmal in Bayern oder Österreich einen vernünftigen Erdäpfelsalat genossen hat, winkt hier ab. Das sollte man dringend hinterfragen.

Schade, wir kamen früher gerne hierher, so allerdings nun nicht mehr. Für Touris reicht das vielleicht irgendwie. Uns konnte es nicht mehr begeistern.

The food was absolutely fantastic. It’s good value for money 64€ for a 5 course and 44€ for the wine pairing, are really reasonable with this outstanding quality of food.

It felt like a very German, straightforward fine dining experience. No bells and whistles, just outstanding ingredients, prepared to the point, with a little twist. Accompanying wine selection was on point as well. Our menu was a take on German and Austrian classics.

The atmosphere felt similarly simplistic German. We went for my wife’s birthday dinner and perhaps were hoping for a more cosy/ romantic experience. I could imagine the outside seating giving a different ambience, but inside downstairs for us wasn’t it. Of course this is something subjective and others will feel differently.

All in all we had a good time and liked the interpretations, but the atmosphere wasn’t for us. I would also recommend taking the 7 course 95€ menu, as I could have easily eaten more.

text:
I've been coming here regularly for over 10 years and have never regretted it :)

The quality has always been top-notch, and no matter what I've eaten, it's always been delicious. To be able to offer that consistently for so many years is quite an achievement. So, kudos to the kitchen! The portions are generous; I often even take some home with me. The value for money is excellent.

My personal favorites are Palak Paneer (probably the best in town) and Butter Chicken.

The service staff has always been friendly and attentive.

The only thing I'm not a big fan of is the background music, but that's a matter of taste, as they say.

The noise level is perfectly fine; you can easily have a conversation even when it's busy.

Larger groups should make a reservation, otherwise, you can usually find a table.

So, if you like Pakistani/North Indian cuisine, you'll love Chelany—a definite recommendation!
originalText:
Seit über 10 Jahren komm ich regelmäßig hier her und hab es noch nie bereut :)
Die Qualität ist immer top gewesen und egal was ich bisher gegessen habe, es war immer lecker. Das so konstant anbieten zu können über viele Jahre hinweg, das muss man erstmal schaffen. Also großes Lob an die Küche. Die Portionen sind ordentlich, oft nehm ich sogar noch was für Zuhause mit. Preis/Leistung ist also sehr gut.
Mein persönlichen Favoriten sind Palak Paneer (wahrscheinlich das beste der Stadt) und Butter Chicken.
Service Personal ist immer freundlich und zuvorkommend gewesen.
Einzig die musikalische Untermalung begeistert mich nicht, aber das ist bekanntlich Geschmackssache.
Geräuschpegel ist völlig in Ordnung, man kann sich angenehm unterhalten auch wenn's voller ist.
Größere Gruppen sollten reservieren, sonst findet sich meist ein Plätzchen.
Also wer pakistanische/nordindische Küche mag, wird das Chelany lieben, eine klare Empfehlung!

placeDescription: Deli platters, steak tartare & mussels, plus creative cocktails, in a hip space with retro stylings.
text:
⭐☆☆☆☆

Our anniversary was supposed to be an unforgettable evening – unfortunately, it became unforgettable for all the wrong reasons. We have rarely left a restaurant so disappointed.

Although we had a reservation, we were completely ignored for about 15 minutes at the entrance. The table was right next to the kitchen, and the music was so loud that conversation was nearly impossible – romantic atmosphere? Forget about it.

First, we were practically pressured to order, and then it seemed we had been completely forgotten. Waiting over an hour for the appetizer is already unacceptable. Waiting almost two hours for the main course, only to find out that the salmon fillet we ordered was no longer available, was the last straw. How can a dish even be ordered if the kitchen hasn't had it in stock?

After more than two hours, we left hungry and frustrated – without a main course. We still had to pay almost €35. Our actual restaurant visit ended up at McDonald's because at least there we could be sure of getting something to eat. That pretty much says it all.

The "compensation" consisted of a supposed Prosecco, which tasted more like heavily diluted white wine with bubbles. A gesture that made the evening even more absurd than it was worth.

The absolute low point came afterward: That same evening (July 10th), my companion sent an email, which, as of today, July 16th, remains unanswered. So you can see that the absolutely abysmal service doesn't end when you leave the restaurant.

Mistakes can happen to anyone. But making guests wait for hours, taking orders that can't possibly be fulfilled, completely ruining a special occasion, and then playing dead is the height of disrespect.

For us, this wasn't just a bad restaurant visit, but one of the worst dining experiences ever. There will definitely be no second visit.
originalText:
⭐☆☆☆☆

Unser Jahrestag sollte ein unvergesslicher Abend werden – leider wurde er unvergesslich aus den völlig falschen Gründen. Selten haben wir ein Restaurant mit so viel Enttäuschung verlassen.

Obwohl wir reserviert hatten, wurden wir am Eingang erst einmal rund 15 Minuten komplett ignoriert. Der Tisch befand sich direkt neben der Küche, die Musik war so laut, dass man sich kaum unterhalten konnte – romantische Atmosphäre? Fehlanzeige.

Zunächst wurden wir regelrecht zum Bestellen gedrängt, danach schien man uns komplett vergessen zu haben. Über eine Stunde auf die Vorspeise zu warten, ist schon eine Zumutung. Fast zwei Stunden auf das Hauptgericht zu warten, nur um dann zu erfahren, dass das bestellte Lachsfilet gar nicht mehr verfügbar ist, schlägt dem Fass den Boden aus. Wie kann ein Gericht überhaupt noch bestellt werden, wenn die Küche längst nichts mehr davon hat?

Nach über zwei Stunden sind wir hungrig und frustriert gegangen – ohne Hauptgericht. Bezahlen durften wir trotzdem knapp 35 €. Unser eigentlicher Restaurantbesuch endete schließlich bei McDonald’s, weil wir dort wenigstens sicher sein konnten, überhaupt etwas zu essen zu bekommen. Das sagt wohl alles.

Die “Wiedergutmachung” bestand aus einem angeblichen Prosecco, der eher wie stark verdünnter Weißwein mit Sprudel schmeckte. Eine Geste, die den Abend eher noch absurder machte als ihn zu retten.

Der absolute Tiefpunkt kam danach: Noch am selben Abend (10.07.) hat meine Begleitung eine Email geschrieben worauf es bis heute dem 16.7 keine Antwort gab. Man merkt also das der absolut Bodenlose Service nicht beim verlassen der Tür aufhört.

Fehler können jedem passieren. Aber Gäste stundenlang warten zu lassen, Bestellungen anzunehmen, die gar nicht erfüllt werden können, einen besonderen Anlass komplett zu ruinieren und sich anschließend totzustellen, ist an Respektlosigkeit kaum zu überbieten.

Für uns war das nicht einfach ein schlechter Restaurantbesuch, sondern eines der schlechtesten Gastronomie-Erlebnisse überhaupt. Ein zweites Mal wird es definitiv nicht geben
ownerResponseText:
We take criticism seriously. However, in this case, the events you described demonstrably do not correspond to what actually happened.

Your reservation was for 9:00 PM. According to our booking system and our maître d', you arrived 16 minutes after your reservation time. Our point-of-sale system shows that your bill was paid at 10:37 PM, as is also evident on the receipt you emailed us. Therefore, the alleged wait times of over two hours are objectively unfounded.

It is not uncommon for guests to have to wait briefly upon arrival until a table is prepared or becomes available in a busy restaurant. However, this does not mean they are being deliberately ignored. In your email, you yourself state that you were told at the entrance that someone would be with you shortly. In your public review, however, you claim to have been ignored for 15 minutes. This contradicts your own account.

We have received your email. Due to the significant contradictions and the impression that a free compensation was being sought despite demonstrably false claims, we have decided against further correspondence.

It is also striking that two very similar one-star reviews were published almost simultaneously and mutually rated as helpful. Unfortunately, this gives the impression that there was a deliberate attempt to damage our rating profile instead of objectively describing the restaurant experience.

That evening, we welcomed well over 100 guests who enjoyed their time with us. We are pleased that we were able to provide a pleasant experience for the numerous other guests, even though we unfortunately cannot meet the expectations of every single guest.

Constructive and honest criticism is always welcome, as it is the only way we can improve. However, false statements and personal attacks are not a basis for this.

We wish you all the best for the future and hope you find a restaurant that meets your expectations.

text:
⭐☆☆☆☆

Our anniversary was supposed to be a special evening – instead, it was by far one of the worst restaurant experiences we've ever had.

Despite having a reservation, we were ignored for 15 minutes at the entrance. The table was right next to the kitchen, and the music was so loud that conversation was nearly impossible. First, we were pressured to order, then ignored for ages. We waited over an hour for the appetizer and almost two hours for the main course, only to find out afterward that the salmon fillet we'd ordered wasn't even available. After more than two hours in the restaurant! How can a dish even be ordered if it's no longer available?

In the end, we left the restaurant without a main course, still paid €35, and then had to go to McDonald's just to get something to eat. The "apology" consisted of a supposed Prosecco that tasted more like white wine diluted with sparkling water.

The worst part: That same evening (July 10th), I sent the restaurant a detailed email. As of today (July 16th), I haven't even received a reply. Apparently, the poor service doesn't end at the restaurant door.

Mistakes can happen. However, making guests wait for hours, taking orders that didn't exist, completely ruining a special occasion, and then not even following up is simply disrespectful.

This will definitely be our first and last visit.

text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Warm, fresh, and simply delicious!

During a major sporting event, my companion and I ate here twice within a week – and both visits were a complete success!

Each time, we were greeted warmly and politely, served attentively, and enjoyed comfortable seating. My two dogs were also warmly welcomed. 🐾❤️ As a little treat from the kitchen, we even received a falafel – a truly lovely and thoughtful touch!

What I also really appreciated was the fantastic selection on the menu. There are several delicious options, so there's something for everyone. I especially liked that the food is freshly prepared, and you can definitely taste the difference. Fresh ingredients, beautiful presentation, and overall, you just get the feeling that good food is a priority here. Absolutely top-notch! 👌🏼

On our second visit, I also had the opportunity to chat a bit longer with the owner and his friends. I learned that the restaurant had only been open for about a month at that point. And honestly, they're already doing a fantastic job!

What I found particularly appealing was that the owner openly asked for my suggestions for improvement and was genuinely interested in feedback. This openness and the passion with which they're building something new really surprised me in a positive way.

Of course, in such a young restaurant, things might still need some fine-tuning. But I completely understood that – and we personally didn't experience any excessively long wait times at all. We simply waited patiently until it was our turn. ☺️

My conclusion: A young, friendly restaurant with a dedicated team, fresh ingredients, delicious food, and an owner who is truly passionate about building something great. Add to that a pleasant atmosphere and a warm welcome – even with a dog. 🐶

When I'm back in Berlin, this is definitely the place I'll be coming back to! ❤️

I give it a clear 5 stars and an absolute recommendation! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
originalText:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Herzlich, frisch und einfach richtig gut!

Während einer Großsportveranstaltung war ich innerhalb einer Woche gleich zweimal mit meiner Begleitung hier essen – und beide Besuche waren rundum positiv!

Wir wurden jedes Mal super freundlich und höflich begrüßt, aufmerksam bedient und konnten uns über einen gemütlichen Sitzplatz freuen. Auch meine beiden Hunde waren herzlich willkommen. 🐾❤️ Als kleinen Gruß aus der Küche gab es sogar eine Falafel – eine wirklich schöne und sympathische Geste!

Was mir ebenfalls sehr gut gefallen hat, war die tolle Auswahl auf der Speisekarte. Es gibt verschiedene, richtig leckere Möglichkeiten, sodass wirklich für unterschiedliche Geschmäcker etwas dabei ist. Besonders positiv fand ich, dass die Speisen frisch zubereitet werden und man das auch schmeckt. Frische Zutaten, eine schöne Präsentation und insgesamt einfach das Gefühl, dass hier Wert auf gutes Essen gelegt wird. Ganz klar: top! 👌🏼

Bei unserem zweiten Besuch hatte ich außerdem die Gelegenheit, mich etwas länger mit dem Besitzer und seinen Freunden zu unterhalten. Dabei habe ich erfahren, dass das Restaurant zu diesem Zeitpunkt erst seit etwa einem Monat geöffnet hatte. Und ganz ehrlich: Dafür machen sie bereits einen richtig tollen Job!

Was ich besonders sympathisch fand: Der Besitzer hat mich ganz offen nach Verbesserungsvorschlägen gefragt und war wirklich interessiert an Feedback. Diese Offenheit und die Leidenschaft, mit der hier etwas Neues aufgebaut wird, haben mich wirklich positiv überrascht.

Natürlich darf sich in einem so jungen Restaurant an der einen oder anderen Stelle noch etwas einspielen. Aber genau dafür hatte ich vollstes Verständnis – wobei wir persönlich überhaupt keine übermäßig langen Wartezeiten hatten. Wir haben einfach entspannt gewartet, bis wir an der Reihe waren. ☺️

Mein Fazit: Ein junges, sympathisches Restaurant mit einem engagierten Team, frischen Lebensmitteln, leckerem Essen und einem Besitzer, der wirklich Lust darauf hat, etwas Gutes aufzubauen. Dazu eine angenehme Atmosphäre und ein herzliches Willkommen – auch mit Hund. 🐶

Wenn ich wieder in Berlin bin, ist das definitiv meine Adresse zum Wiederkommen! ❤️

Von mir gibt es ganz klar 5 Sterne und eine absolute Empfehlung! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

text:
⭐⭐⭐☆☆

The food was absolutely delicious and the quality was excellent. I was all the more surprised, then, to find out when it was time to pay that they only accepted cash. Unfortunately, there was no indication of this at the entrance, on the menu, or anywhere else.

As a result, I had to walk quite a distance to an ATM, withdraw cash, and then return to pay the bill. Furthermore, I wasn't given a receipt or invoice.

This was all very inconvenient and could easily have been avoided with a simple notice. I hope that card payments will be offered in the future, or at least that it will be clearly indicated that only cash payments are accepted and that receipts will, of course, be issued.
originalText:
⭐⭐⭐☆☆

Das war insgesamt sehr umständlich und hätte sich mit einem einfachen Hinweis leicht vermeiden lassen. Ich hoffe, dass künftig Kartenzahlung angeboten wird oder zumindest deutlich darauf hingewiesen wird, dass nur Barzahlung möglich ist und Rechnungen selbstverständlich ausgestellt werden.

Sfera, Schudomastraße 44, 12055 Berlin, Germany
Sfera, Schudomastraße 44, 12055 Berlin, Germany
text:
Sfera is absolutely worth the trip, even though it’s a little outside the more central parts of Berlin. The space is much bigger than it looks from the outside, bright, welcoming and perfect for a relaxed brunch.

I had an espresso and the French toast, which was incredible. It was topped with fresh fruit, crunchy crumbles and a delicious syrup; easily one of the best brunch dishes with brioche I’ve had in Berlin. They also have a beautiful display of pastries and donuts that all looked amazing.

The menu is fairly small, but everything feels carefully selected (and I believe it’s all vegan). A big plus is that they serve free tap water, which is always appreciated.

The staff were genuinely warm and friendly throughout our visit. I’d definitely recommend making a reservation, as it’s a popular spot. There are only a couple of seats outside, so it’s mainly an indoor café, but the atmosphere inside more than makes up for it.

A fantastic brunch spot that I’ll definitely be coming back to.

text:
March 2026: After further visits, I stand by my initial assessment below without reservation. It was a culinary experience every time.

2024: Today I visited the "Alte Wäscherei" (Old Laundry) for the first time and was pleasantly surprised. An Italian restaurant with a small menu that changes weekly. They offer lunch and dinner. text:
Once you find the entrance in the typical second courtyard, you'll find yourself in a large, bright space in what was once a laundry. Three of the four courses, in particular, were so interestingly combined that you won't find them everywhere. You could definitely be a bit more imaginative with the dessert, guys, but it was tasty nonetheless.

Overall, a really great lunch and a wonderful birthday invitation from a good friend. I would absolutely recommend it.

text:
I had a really lovely experience at this Italian restaurant. We started with a piadina filled with scamorza and salame, and another with prosciutto — both were absolutely delicious, rich in flavor and perfectly balanced.
For the main courses, we ordered the tagliatelle with sausage and the tagliatelle with pistachio. Everything was outstanding. You can truly taste the difference: the pasta is handmade, and it shows in both texture and flavor.
With great surprise, I also found an Aperol Spritz on the menu for only €5 — such an unexpected an amazing price.
One of the most special aspects of this place is the open kitchen. There’s a visible cooking area where you can actually see the fire and watch the dishes being prepared, which adds a really authentic and cozy touch to the whole experience.
The service was exceptionally kind and attentive throughout the entire meal, which made the experience even more enjoyable.
The dining room is a bit small, so I would definitely recommend making a reservation in advance. Overall, a fantastic spot for anyone looking for genuine, high-quality Italian food.

text:
We sat in the beer garden by the street, which was pleasant. The noise level inside was so high that we asked them to close a window right by our table.

There was a mix-up with the drinks order; to err is human. I was very pleased that they also had a non-alcoholic pilsner (Jever) on tap.

The food—roulade, liver, sauerkraut—was, frankly, awful.

The sauerkraut looked unpleasantly like straw; it was dry and bland. I've never seen or eaten anything like it, not even canned.

The roulade had an off taste; it was sour, as if it had been seasoned incorrectly or preserved in some way, and tasted like stale meat. The texture was terrible: no bite at all; the filling was complete mush. I can't describe it any other way.

Then there was the calf's liver. It also tasted bland, and somehow different from real liver. We couldn't tell if it was calf's liver. The hot dogs came with fried onions, which were larger than those you'd find on supermarket hot dogs, but tasted and textured exactly the same.

The service was quite attentive, but seemed somewhat unprofessional. In the kitchen (the restaurant wasn't very busy), mobile phones were clearly essential.

While the food is quite cheap, the quality is unfortunately equally poor. Therefore, I can hardly comment on the value for money.

Unfortunately, it wasn't a particularly memorable experience that we would return to, which is a shame. Berlin cuisine is becoming increasingly rare and would be a good fit for this location.
originalText:
Wir haben uns in den Biergarten an der Straße gesetzt, was angenehm war. Der Geräuschpegel innen war so laut, das wir baten, ein Fensterdirekt bei uns zu schließen.
Bei der Getränke Bestellung kam es zu einer Verwechselung, irren ist menschlich. Sehr positiv finde ich, daß es auch ein alkoholfreies Pils (Jever) vom Fass gibt.
Das Essen, Roulade, Leber, Sauerkraut, war ehrlich gesagt nichts.
Das Sauerkraut sah schon unangenehm wie Stroh aus, es war trocken und fade. So etwas habe ich noch nie gesehen und gegessen, nicht mal aus der Dose.
Die Roulade war geschmacklich falsch, sie war säuerlich, als ob sie falsch gewürzt oder irgend wie haltbar gemacht wurde, schmeckte nach Leege. Die Konsistenz war: kein Biss, die Füllung war kompletter Matsch, das kann ich leider nicht anders beschreiben.
Dann war da noch die Kalbsleber. Die schmeckte ebenfalls fade, auch irgend wie anders als richtige Leber. Ob es sich um Kalbsleber handelte, konnten wir nicht rausschmecken. Dazu gab es Röstzwiebeln, welche größer waren als die fertige HotDog-Ware aus dem Supermarkt, aber in Geschmack und Konsistenz dieser genau gleichte.
Die Bedienung war eher häufig present, wirkte aber etwas unprofessionell. In der Küche (das Lokal war nicht so voll) war das Handy sehr wichtig.
Die Essen sind zwar recht billig, leider aber erst recht deren Qualität. Somit kann ich kaum über ein Preis/Leistungsverhälnis schreiben.
Das war leider kein besonderes Erlebnis, zu dem wir wiederholt erscheinen würden, schade. Berliner Küche ist ja sonst selten geworden und würde an diesen Platz gut passen.

text:
I always try to keep my reviews objective and give others an honest impression. This time, however, it's difficult not to sound harsh: this was probably the worst restaurant meal I have ever had.

For €15, you get a few spoonfuls of mostly cold, sour, and poorly seasoned vegetables served on soggy injera, plus more injera on the side. Three people paid almost €50 for what was essentially lentils, cabbage, pumpkin, and a few supermarket salad leaves.

The service was friendly, but unfortunately, no owner was available to discuss the criticism. In my view, the prices are completely unjustified given the very poor quality.

Generally speaking, I always try to remain objective in my reviews and give other customers and guests an authentic impression so they can form their own opinion before visiting. I've never found this so difficult, because in this case, objectivity comes across as very stark: probably the worst meal I've ever had in a restaurant. Far too expensive! For €15 you get five tablespoons of what is essentially cold, sour, and blandly seasoned vegetables, served on soggy flatbreads. They also provide more flatbreads to eat with the meal. This is typical of Ethiopian cuisine in the Lippe region of Germany. In other words, you're paying almost €50 for food that wasn't even reheated for three people. It's a shame I didn't take a picture. All I got was a few lentils, bread, yellow cabbage, kale, pumpkin, and three small lettuces from the supermarket. The only redeeming feature was the friendly service. Unfortunately, the owner wasn't available, so I had to voice my strong criticism there, to no avail. Everyone should consider beforehand whether they want to support this outrageous pricing in light of the abysmal quality.

Grundsätzlich: ich versuche in meinen Besprechungen immer objektiv zu bleiben und anderen Kunden und Gästen einen authentischen Eindruck zu vermitteln, damit sie selber möglichst vor dem Besuch sich ein Bild machen können. Noch nie ist mir das so schwer gefallen, weil in diesem Falle Objektivität sehr krass rüberkommt: das wohl schlechteste Essen in einem Restaurant das ich in meinem Leben hatte. Viel zu teuer! Für 15 € bekommt man fünf Esslöffel eigentlich kaltes, säuerliches, nicht interessant gewürztes Gemüse, serviert auf aufgeweichten Fladen, zusätzlich gibt es auch noch Fladen zum Essen. Das ist ja landes lippisch für äthiopische Küche. D.h. man hat für noch nicht einmal aufgewärmtes Essen für drei Personen praktisch 50 € zu bezahlen, schade dass ich kein Foto gemacht habe, für ein paar Linsen Brot und gelb, Grünkohl, Kürbis, drei kleine Blattsalat aus dem Supermarkt, das einzig erfreuliche war die nette Bedienung. Leider war kein Besitzer zu sprechen, so musste ich meine deutliche Kritik erfolglos dort anbringen. Es möge sich jeder vorher überlegen, ob er diese angesichts der unterirdischen Qualität unverschämte Preisgestaltung mittragen möchte.

text: I can't praise this restaurant enough! My best friend and I visited for the first time in July 2026 and received a very warm welcome. We arrived right at 3:00 PM and were able to choose our own tables, but I would recommend making a reservation for 5:00 or 6:00 PM onwards. The owner has fantastic energy and is always happy to answer any questions. He took plenty of time for us and introduced us to the wide variety of dishes. I also have to mention that the restrooms are very well-maintained and clean, which is always very important to me. The corn fufu wasn't really to my taste, but the owner explained that there are many other types of fufu and that they taste different, so I wouldn't say that's a negative at all; I would simply attribute it to my personal preference. Otherwise, the food was incredibly delicious, and the restaurant's history was very interesting. I would highly recommend this restaurant, especially for the friendliness and the atmosphere. It's also only a 5-minute walk from Hermannstraße train station. So, thank you again for the warm welcome!

text:
World Cup. Germany vs Ecuador.

It looked closed when we got there. Even if this was Neukölln it was past 10pm. But seeing us at the door, they smiled and said come in, the kitchen can still cook one more dinner. The game was on anyway.

Food was delicious: the oxtail and the cassava leaf stews were hearty.  We ate “African style” like was suggested. With fofo to dip and a bowl of cool water to wet/rinse out fingers.

We even watched the game. And we don’t watch football. But we were happy we did that night. And happy to tell everyone to come and visit our new favorite spot in this area.

On a side note: someone came in and said she just wanted to watch the game. And if she could just order some plantains? “Fierabend,” they said. We couldn’t finish ours so we offered it to her. “I’ll get you something to eat that with,” our new friend told her. She smiled and sat down, while we went home before the game finished

text:
We went to Next Level and ordered fufu with peanut sauce and rice. The fufu and sauce tasted good overall. However, the rice was very dry.

Unfortunately, I found a hair in my portion of fufu relatively early on. I pointed it out to the owner. He wanted to see the hair himself, then even pulled it out of the fufu and apologized. Understandably, he seemed shocked by the incident.

After this experience, I couldn't finish my meal.

What I found particularly disappointing was how the situation was handled at the end. Despite the obvious mistake, I had to pay the full price. Neither a replacement portion was offered nor was the affected dish removed from the bill.

Mistakes can happen, but in such a case, I would have expected a more accommodating solution. In the future, it would be nice if guests were at least offered a replacement or not charged for the dish in such cases.

placeDescription: Stylish specialist venue for artfully designed & presented desserts, plus wine pairings & cocktails.
text:
I visited Coda now that they're in Copenhagen for the month.
I've done my fair share of Michelin fine dining, and this is the first one-star rating that I give.
I've left the table feeling utterly baffled at how this restaurant can hold two Michelin stars and be in the World's 50 Best Restaurants.
The whole menu feels like a collection of ingredients forcefully assembled onto a plate with the sole purpose of proving that a non-conformist, dessert-like tasting menu can exist. Maybe it can, but certainly not this way.
To me, nothing of what makes a Michelin-starred menu truly memorable was present. Despite what they claim on their website about balance, every dish was heavily and inevitably tilted towards sweetness, while savory, salty, umami, acidic rich and fatty were almost entirely absent. Even ingredients like shiitake, kombu, shiso and miso, which are kings of umami, were completely muted and seemed to be fighting in vain against the overwhelming sweetness. Ultimately, what makes a tasting menu stay with you is how impossibly delicious the food is. No amount of technique or philosophy can salvage a menu where the dominant thought at every bite is simply, "sweet." And perhaps the clearest indication of this is that, less than 24 hours later, I have already forgotten virtually all of the dishes in terms of their flavors and ingredients. Nothing has really stayed with me.
I ended the evening craving something salty, which, to me, is never a good sign when leaving a Michelin restaurant.
Great dishes can also excel through appearance, aroma and texture, but none of those elevated the experience either. The presentation lacked striking colours or particularly beautiful compositions, the dishes were aromatically muted, and the textures rarely offered much contrast.
The menu was also very repetitive. Every single dish included an ice cream component, which also provided the only temperature contrast throughout the meal. Almost every dish lacked a sauce, and every dish lacked the harmony that transforms individual ingredients into something greater than the sum of their parts. The same disconnection was present in the juice pairing: rather than complementing or creating a dialogue with the food, the juices felt disconnected from the menu, in much the same way that the individual ingredients within each dish felt disconnected from one another. They also brought even more sweetness to a meal where the sweetness of the food was already becoming extremely tiring. The only three dishes that weren't overwhelmingly sweet were essentially variations on the same idea: a carbohydrate base (a doughnut, a tart and a waffle) filled with molten cheese - not even particularly distinctive cheeses, just regular ones like Gouda.
The thing that upsets me the most, though, is the restaurant's self-proclaimed boundary-pushing pâtisserie philosophy, which, as far as I could tell, boiled down to ice cream in most dishes, chocolate everywhere (by the final chocolate course I was completely tired of it), aquafaba meringue, cake batter, waffles and a soufflé/tart. Any amateur baker who's watched Bake Off has experimented with these techniques at home (which are at the very basis of approaching bakery), to varying degrees of success, and certainly not for €300 or with two Michelin stars attached.
I do appreciate that, halfway through the meal, the team tried to salvage my experience by serving me an extra dish they thought would better match my preference for savory, acidic and umami flavours. It was a genuinely thoughtful gesture. Unfortunately, that dish only reinforced my impression that the menu as a whole was overwhelmingly sweet and fundamentally unbalanced.
I understand this is a very harsh review, but I've tried to keep it grounded in specific observations, and I hope it's clear that it's nothing personal.
But to me, what they say on their website - "What started as a dessert bar" - can only be completed with: "should have stayed a dessert bar".

text:
Fine dining frequently degenerates into a transactional theater of status. You do not secure a table to experience culinary architecture, but rather you secure it to prove you possess the capital to do so. Consequently, you are obligated to take the pictures, broadcast the event to your friends, and perform the entire socioeconomic ritual. Profound hospitality occurs when a restaurant actively dismantles that dynamic.

Let me recount an anecdote that remains the greatest walk-in experience we have ever executed. It happened here, several years ago, precisely the night after the establishment was awarded its first Michelin star. A party of three attempted a late-night walk-in. They anchored us directly at the bar.
On that specific night, the barrier of not having a reservation did not exist. It was not a matter of slamming a black Amex on the host stand to force access. We came late, and we stayed late. We were the final guests remaining in the room, deeply fascinated by René Frank's laboratory-grade assembly.

What captivated us most was the strict discipline of the menu. Although operating entirely within the parameters of dessert, the absolute absence of refined sugar—relying instead on the natural extraction of sweetness—was a masterclass that provided a breathtaking glimpse into the future of the discipline.

Then came the check. The card was processed. It failed. It failed a second time, inducing a highly specific cold sweat. The universal, nervous joke in this scenario is that you will be sent to the back to wash the dishes. And that's exactly where we were escorted after the transaction eventually cleared on a subsequent attempt. But the mechanical resolution of the bill is irrelevant, and the sink was not our destination. What remains permanent is the restaurant's reaction.

They recognized our genuine fascination with their craft. They saw individuals for whom food is a real passion, not a hollow status symbol. We were escorted behind the counter and directly into their studio where the brigade was cleaning down after service, still running on the pure adrenaline of their newly minted star. They invited us into the center of their operational matrix and showed us their work simply because we cared about the mechanics of it. It was an absolute masterclass in unpretentious hospitality. Typical Berlin experience.

text: Got food poisoning after the tasting menu with alcohol pairing in 2017. When I reached out, the restaurant denied any responsibility, claimed no one else had the same issue, and asked for a doctor’s note instead of simply apologizing. Not the response you’d expect from a place of this caliber.
ownerResponseText:
Dear Daria,

Thank you for getting in touch again after nine years.

We already emailed you back then to express our condolences. That evening, the restaurant was occupied by 50 other guests, and we contacted everyone to find out if they had experienced the same thing as you. They hadn't, and we informed you of this. We didn't receive any further response from you to that email, so we were unable to investigate the matter further. After nine years, it is unfortunately no longer possible for us to reliably reconstruct the events from that time or to change anything.

Best regards,

The CODA Team
ownerResponseOriginalText:
Liebe Daria, 

Vielen Dank, dass du dich nach 9 Jahren noch einmal meldest. 
Wir haben dir damals bereits eine E-Mail geschrieben und unser Mitgefühl mitgeteilt. An diesem Abend war das Restaurant mit weiteren 50 Gästen besetzt und wir haben alle kontaktiert um herauszufinden, ob es ihnen genauso erging wie euch. Dies war nicht der Fall und darüber haben wir euch informiert. Auf diese E-Mail haben wir keine weitere Rückmeldung von Euch erhalten, sodass wir den Fall nicht weiter klären konnten. Nach nunmehr neun Jahren ist es für uns leider nicht mehr möglich, den damaligen Sachverhalt verlässlich nachzuvollziehen oder noch etwas daran zu ändern.

Beste Grüße,

Das CODA-Team

text: We've eaten Pad Thai here many times. The place used to be a great option for affordable Pad Thai. With the obvious change of ownership, that's no longer the case for us. We usually take the rest of the large portion to go – it's never been a problem before. This time, the owner (or the owner's daughter? – she was frequently on the phone with her father and complained, among other things, that the staff always give us such a late notice when they're running low on something – that already made us feel uneasy)... anyway, they're now charging extra for packing up leftovers. When I asked if it would cost an extra euro to take away, I only got a curt reply. The former owners, the cute Asian couple, still work there – but are now being bossed around by a young woman who doesn't seem to have much experience in customer service. When we pointed out that this rip-off with the packing was rather off-putting for us as regular customers, the only response was that we could go somewhere else in the future - and that's exactly what we'll do!

Mae Chaeron has to be one of my favourite places to eat in Berlin and in Neukölln especially. Great food, super quick, not expensive at all (especially for the quantity, sometimes it's like two meals) and miles better than most Asian restaurants around the same price point. It can be tough to get a place to sit there sometimes, but if you're getting something to go, it's always a good shout.

The Kau Pat (fried rice) is my personal favourite but the Pad Thai is fantastic and so are all the curries, soups and the menu in general.

I've probably been there 50+ times at this point and it rarely, if ever, disappoints.

Huge thank you to the Thai aunties of Sonnenallee - we love you!

ownerResponseText:
Thank you for your positive review and the praise for our Pad Grapao Ped, Tom Yam, and our service.

We appreciate your feedback regarding the spiciness. We know from experience that many guests order "Thai spicy" but often significantly underestimate the actual spiciness of an authentic Thai dish. In the past, this has frequently led to dishes being perceived as too spicy and having to be prepared again.

For this reason, we strive to find a balanced level of spiciness. For those who prefer it even spicier, we offer various toppings such as chili powder and other seasonings next to our counter. This allows each guest to adjust the spiciness to their own taste.

Please feel free to ask us directly on your next visit if you would like a particularly authentic Thai spiciness. We look forward to seeing you again.
ownerResponseOriginalText:
Vielen Dank für Ihre positive Bewertung und das Lob für unser Pad Grapao Ped, die Tom Yam und unseren Service.

Ihren Hinweis zur Schärfe nehmen wir gerne auf. Aus Erfahrung wissen wir, dass „thai scharf“ von vielen Gästen bestellt wird, die tatsächliche Schärfe eines authentisch thailändischen Gerichts dann aber oft deutlich unterschätzen. In der Vergangenheit kam es deshalb häufiger vor, dass Gerichte als zu scharf empfunden wurden und neu zubereitet werden mussten.

Aus diesem Grund versuchen wir, bei der Schärfe eine ausgewogene Balance zu finden. Für alle, die es gerne noch schärfer mögen, stehen neben unserem Tresen verschiedene Toppings wie Chilipulver und weitere Würzmittel bereit. So kann jeder Gast den Schärfegrad individuell an den eigenen Geschmack anpassen.

Gerne können Sie uns bei Ihrem nächsten Besuch auch direkt ansprechen, wenn Sie eine besonders authentische thailändische Schärfe wünschen. Wir freuen uns auf Ihren nächsten Besuch

text:
I stumbled upon Rusticana quite by chance and was pleasantly surprised. I only intended to grab a quick bite, but the €10 lunch menu was definitely worth it. The pork neck steak was beautifully juicy, the creamy mushroom sauce was delicious, and the rosemary potatoes were perfectly crispy. It came with a fresh salad and, to top it all off, a panna cotta that was the perfect finishing touch.

I especially appreciated the complimentary olives and fresh bread beforehand, and even a free espresso after the meal. It's these little touches that make all the difference for me.

Afterwards, I ordered an ice cream sundae, which was also delicious. The ice cream was wonderfully creamy, the portion was generous, and the whipped cream tasted fresh. The only slight downside was that it was a bit noisy at times due to the other guests, but that's not the restaurant's fault.

Overall, a very enjoyable visit with delicious food, friendly service, and a price that's hard to find these days. I'll definitely be back.

placeAddress: Rusticana, Hermannstraße 152, 12051 Berlin, Germany
text:
I pick up my grandma from the nursing home next door once or twice a week, and we usually go to Rusticana for lunch together. So we've been there quite a few times.

What we particularly like is the lunch special. For 8 to 10 euros, you get an appetizer, a main course, and even dessert. The dishes change regularly; sometimes there's fish, sometimes liver, sometimes something else. With an apple spritzer, I usually pay around 13.50 euros. For what you get, I think that's really great.

We also like the pizzas. Occasionally, they're a bit too dark, but we've always been satisfied with the taste.

It's also important to us that the restaurant is accessible. There's a wheelchair ramp at the entrance, so my grandma can get in without any problems. There's also an accessible restroom, even with a grab bar. It seems a bit loose, though, and could use a check-up.

At lunchtime, it can sometimes get quite crowded and therefore a bit noisy. The restaurant is a popular meeting place, especially for many guests from the Balkans, who enjoy sitting together, drinking coffee, and chatting. The atmosphere is usually warm and convivial. However, if you – like us – simply want to eat in peace and enjoy the company, it can occasionally be a bit hectic. But that's just our personal experience, and certainly not a problem for many others.

Ultimately, the positive aspects clearly outweigh the negative for us. My grandmother feels comfortable there, knows the dishes, and is always happy when we go. And that's what matters most to me. Therefore, we will continue to be regular customers.
originalText:
Ich hole meine Oma ein- bis zweimal pro Woche aus dem Pflegeheim direkt nebenan ab, und meistens gehen wir dann zusammen ins Rusticana essen. Deshalb sind wir schon ziemlich oft dort gewesen.

Was uns besonders gefällt, ist das Mittagsangebot. Für 8 bis 10 Euro bekommt man eine Vorspeise, einen Hauptgang und sogar noch ein Dessert. Die Gerichte wechseln regelmäßig, mal gibt es Fisch, mal Leber, mal etwas anderes. Mit einer Apfelschorle zahle ich meistens um die 13,50 Euro. Für das, was man bekommt, finde ich das wirklich top.

Die Pizzen schmecken uns auch gut. Ab und zu sind sie zwar etwas zu dunkel geraten, aber geschmacklich waren wir trotzdem immer zufrieden.

Für uns ist außerdem wichtig, dass das Restaurant barrierefrei ist. Es gibt eine Rollstuhlrampe am Eingang, sodass meine Oma problemlos hineinkommt. Auch eine Behindertentoilette ist vorhanden, sogar mit Haltegriff. Der wirkt allerdings etwas locker und könnte bei Gelegenheit mal überprüft werden.

Zur Mittagszeit kann es manchmal recht voll und entsprechend auch etwas lauter werden. Das Restaurant ist ein beliebter Treffpunkt, unter anderem für viele Gäste aus den Balkanländern, die dort gerne zusammen sitzen, Kaffee trinken und sich unterhalten. Die Stimmung ist dabei meistens herzlich und gesellig. Wenn man allerdings – so wie wir – einfach mal in Ruhe essen und die gemeinsame Zeit genießen möchte, kann es gelegentlich etwas anstrengend werden. Das ist aber nur unser persönliches Empfinden und sicherlich für viele andere überhaupt kein Problem.

Am Ende überwiegen für uns ganz klar die positiven Dinge. Meine Oma fühlt sich dort wohl, kennt die Gerichte und freut sich jedes Mal, wenn wir hingehen. Und genau das ist für mich eigentlich das Wichtigste. Deshalb werden wir auch weiterhin regelmäßig vorbeischauen.

text:
Yesterday, the two of us ate at Portofino.

Visually, it's an appealing place with an open kitchen.

It started off well with a very good cappuccino.

The service was okay. However, the staff seemed like they were just going through the motions. None of the waiters had a smile on their face. They all seemed very tense. The antipasti were average, nothing special. I had a chicken salad for €30. A hefty price, especially since the menu promised a Parmesan dressing.

What a joke! It arrived with about 10 small lettuce leaves, nothing else. No onions, corn, or any of the other ingredients that make a salad. Just the lettuce leaves. The dressing didn't taste like Parmesan at all, nor was it visible. Just a few drops scattered on the lettuce leaves. There was a tomato bruschetta on the side, a nice idea, but the toasted bread was unfortunately cold and hard.

I sent the plate back and didn't try again.

The tiramisu was good.

The fact that we were still charged for the salad would normally warrant a one-star rating.

However, since we didn't try any other dishes, that wouldn't be appropriate.
originalText:
Waren gestern zu zweit im Portofino Essen.
Optisch ein ansprechender Ort mit offener Küche.
Fing auch gut an mit einem sehr guten Cappuccino.
Die Bedienung war OK. Allerdings wirkt die Crew eher wie zur Arbeit gezwungen. Keiner der Kellner hatte ein Lächeln im Gesicht. Alle wirkten sehr angespannt. Die Antipasti waren durchschnittlich, nichts besonderes. Hatte einen Salat mit Huhn für 30€. Ein stolzer Preis, dafür versprach die Karte ein Parmesan-Dressing.
Wirklich ein Hohn, es kamen ca 10 kleine Salatblätter, nichts weiter. Keine Zwiebeln, Mais oder sonstige Zutaten die einen Salat ausmachen. Tatsächlich nur die Salatblätter. Das Dressing hat weder nach Parmesan geschmeckt noch war es sichtbar. Ein paar Tröpfchen auf den Salatblättern verteilt. An der Seite war ein Bruschetta mit Tomate, gut gemeint aber das getoastete Brot war leider kalt und hart.
Ich habe das den Teller zurück gehen lassen und auf einen weiteren Versuch verzichtet.
Das Tiramisu war gut.
Das der Salat trotzdem berechnet wurde wäre eigentlich eine ein Sterne Bewertung angebracht.
Aber da wir keine anderen Speisen probiert haben, wäre das nicht angebracht.
ownerResponseText:

Restrooms...

ownerResponseText:
Thank you for your feedback. We take all feedback seriously and continuously evaluate our work.

It's a shame that you overlooked the value of handcrafted products and the significant effort involved in their creation in your review.

There are certainly cheaper alternatives, but quality always comes at a price, and we pay particular attention to this, especially in our meticulous work and the selection of high-quality, fresh ingredients.

Of course, it's entirely up to you whether you recommend us or not, but we didn't find the respect you mentioned reflected in either the comparison to "paper" or the word "disgrace."

Sincerely,

Team Maranda


Sincerely,
ownerResponseOriginalText:
Vielen Dank für das Feedback. Wir nehmen jede Rückmeldung ernst und evaluieren unsere Arbeit fortlaufend.

Schade, dass Sie den Wert von handgefertigten Produkten und den damit verbundenen hohen Aufwand bei Ihrer Bewertung außer Acht gelassen haben.

Es gibt sicherlich günstigere Alternativen aber Qualität hat immer Ihren Preis, und darauf achten wir vor allem bei unserer sauberen Arbeit und der Wahl von hochwertigen und frischen Zutaten.

Es liegt natürlich in Ihrem Ermessen, uns weiterzuempfehlen oder nicht, aber den Respekt, den Sie erwähnen, konnten wir weder in dem Vergleich „wie Papier“ noch in dem Wort „Schande“ wiederfinden.


Mit freundlichen Grüßen,
Team Maranda

text:
I was really keen to try this restaurant because it has so many excellent reviews on Google. That makes my visit all the more disappointing.

I almost always order a Margherita at a new pizzeria because it's the best way to judge the quality. It's the most classic pizza – you can tell how good the dough is and whether they're using high-quality tomato sauce and good cheese.

The dough was indeed really good, but unfortunately, that was the best thing about it. There was hardly any tomato sauce on the pizza and very little cheese. Basically, I mostly ate dough.

It's a shame because the dough really had potential. With a bit more tomato sauce and cheese, the pizza would probably have been significantly better. Given all the positive reviews, I expected much more.

Basically, I just ate dough. The pizza had practically no flavor.
originalText:
Ich wollte dieses Restaurant unbedingt ausprobieren, weil es bei Google so viele hervorragende Bewertungen hat. Umso enttäuschter bin ich von meinem Besuch.

Ich bestelle in einer neuen Pizzeria fast immer eine Margherita, weil man daran die Qualität am besten beurteilen kann. Es ist die klassischste Pizza – daran erkennt man, wie gut der Teig ist und ob hochwertige Tomatensauce und guter Käse verwendet werden.

Der Teig war zwar wirklich gut, aber das war leider auch schon das Beste daran. Auf der Pizza war kaum Tomatensauce und vom Käse nur sehr wenig. Im Grunde habe ich hauptsächlich Teig gegessen.

Schade, denn der Teig hatte wirklich Potenzial. Mit etwas mehr Tomatensauce und Käse wäre die Pizza wahrscheinlich deutlich besser gewesen. Für die vielen positiven Bewertungen hatte ich deutlich mehr erwartet.

Im Grunde habe ich einfach nur Teig gegessen. Die Pizza hatte praktisch keinen Geschmack.

text:
I like it. A lot.

You can order anything from the menu. The coffee is strong, just the way it should be.

The ambiance inside is reminiscent of a Viennese coffee house, so it's perfect for escaping the everyday routine. Sitting outside is fantastic. It's a bit like being in a village. You can people-watch, eavesdrop on neighbors' conversations, and everything seems to move at a slower pace along this street. But my absolute favorite thing about the Goldberg is that they have newspapers and magazines in print. Please keep that up!
originalText:
Ich mag's. Sehr.
Von der Karte kann man alles essen. Der Kaffee stark, so wie er sein muss.
Das Ambiente drinnen erinnert ein bisschen an ein Wiener Kaffeehaus, also perfekt um mal dem Alltag zu entfliehen. Draußen zu sitzen ist ganz großes Kino. Es ist ein bisschen wie auf einem Dorf. Man kann Leute beobachten, Nachbarn bei ihren Gesprächen belauschen und alles scheint an dieser Straßenführung etwas langsamer zu sein. Aber mein absoluter Pluspunkt vom Goldberg ist, sie haben Zeitungen und Magazine in Papierform. Bitte behaltet das bei....
ownerResponseText:
Dear Reviewer,

Thank you so much for your wonderful feedback! We're delighted to hear that you enjoyed both the variety of our menu and our strong coffee. It's lovely to hear that you appreciate our inviting atmosphere and feel like you're in a Viennese coffee house. We're pleased that you enjoy people-watching and the relaxed pace of life on our street. And of course, we will continue to offer printed newspapers and magazines for our guests.

We look forward to your next visit!

Warm regards,
Your Goldberg Team
ownerResponseOriginalText:
Lieber Bewerter,

vielen Dank für dein tolles Feedback! Es freut uns zu hören, dass dir sowohl die Vielfalt unserer Speisekarte als auch der starke Kaffee bei uns gefallen. Es ist schön zu hören, dass du das einladende Ambiente bei uns schätzt und dich wie in einem Wiener Kaffeehaus fühlst. Wir freuen uns, dass du das Beobachten der Menschen und das entschleunigte Tempo auf unserer Straße genießt. Und natürlich werden wir auch weiterhin Zeitungen und Magazine in gedruckter Form für unsere Gäste bereithalten. 

Wir freuen uns bereits auf deinen nächsten Besuch!

Herzliche Grüße,
Dein Team von Goldberg

text:
Hello Kalaja team,

Since your restaurant is one of my favorites, I feel it is important to give you some honest feedback. I would like you to continue to focus on quality, freshness and service in the kitchen and in the restaurant.

For my visit today (lunch):

* Espresso Macchiato: I left it without drinking it because the milk tasted sour and seemed to have been reheated several times.

* Water and Coca-Cola in glass bottles: Are they no longer served in glasses? It seemed like we had to drink straight from the bottle.

* Mix Grill: The kebabs were not cooked well and there were only three small pieces. Also, I had asked for no lamb, but it was still on the plate. That is why I left the food.

* Goulash: It seemed like it was not fresh. We left this dish too.

* Bread: It did not seem fresh, like it was not made that day.

I am very sorry to say this, because I have always had a very good opinion of your restaurant.

Next time I will come in person and introduce myself. I will order the same dishes again and I hope that you will show me the quality for which I have always appreciated you. I hope that you will take this feedback as constructive criticism, because my desire is to continue to be a satisfied customer of your restaurant.
